institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 25, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2018. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published December 2019.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin.
method: Vitek 2 YST antifungal susceptibility cards (bioMerieux, France) and E test, repeat isolates excluded; cumulative antibiogram per CLSI M39-A (printed "CLSI M-39A Vol. 22, No. 8; 2002 (global consensus guidelines)"); interpreted as per CLSI M27-S4 (2012), and the C. albicans breakpoints were used where no species-specific breakpoints are available; C. glabrata voriconazole by an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml (CLSI gives no voriconazole criteria for C. glabrata); amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml.

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then cut into two halves with the species column kept on both: no differences. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 25, No. 2 (published December 2019), data January to December 2018, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2018)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin and micafungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". Footnotes: # C. glabrata: no susceptible category for fluconazole (the row prints "100% SDD", left out) and no voriconazole breakpoints, so an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml was used for voriconazole; ## SDD susceptible dose dependent; C. albicans breakpoints where no species-specific breakpoints are available (noted on the cells concerned); * and ** as before (Vitek 2 YST cards, E test, repeat isolates excluded, CLSI M39-A 2002; amphotericin B as isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml). Flucytosine is back, headed "5 Flucytosine". The text under the table says 14 C. auris isolates from July to September 2019 (as printed, in this 2018 edition; probable hospital-acquired infection) were excluded from the data. The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "December-2019"). The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 47 cells and 8 n: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: C. glabrata fluconazole "100% SDD##" left out with the right note; voriconazole by the 0.25 µg/ml epidemiological cut-off noted; the line under the table "14 isolates of C. auris were isolated between July-Sept 2019 (probable HAI) and were excluded from the data" is recorded (the year 2019 is as printed). Cells not kept, all printed that way: caution C. auris amphotericin B 11.4, flucytosine 45.7 and voriconazole 11.4 with n = 23; intrinsic C. krusei fluconazole 0.
Observation: the three C. auris figures equal 4/35, 16/35 and 4/35 (not 23 + 14 = 37), so they may have been computed on 35 isolates; the page does not say. Added to the row note.
